criteria.text: Breakthrough pain in adult cancer patients already receiving and tolerant to around-the-clock opioid therapy for underlying persistent cancer pain (approval criterion 2 is covered by this closed indication).
Patient is at least 18 years old (approval criterion 1).
Patient is receiving around-the-clock opioid therapy for underlying persistent cancer pain and must remain on this therapy while taking Subsys (approval criterion 4).

Patient is opioid tolerant: at least 60 mg oral morphine daily, 25 mcg/hour transdermal fentanyl, 30 mg oral oxycodone daily, 8 mg oral hydromorphone daily, or an equianalgesic dose of another opioid daily for at least 1 week (approval criterion 3).

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid Subsys (fentanyl sublingual spray). Available strengths: 100, 200, 400, 600, 800, 1200, 1600 mcg.
Source Version 1, Last updated 12/11/2012, Approved 01/18/2013. Extracted effective_date is null; existing effective_date stub 1970-01-01 retained; it is not a stated PDF effective date.

Approval criterion 2 (being treated for cancer pain) is covered by the closed cancer breakthrough pain indication; no separate cancer attestation is required. Criteria 1, 3 and 4 encode adult age, opioid tolerance and around-the-clock opioid therapy.

Patient is opioid tolerant: at least 60 mg oral morphine daily, 25 mcg/hour transdermal fentanyl, 30 mg oral oxycodone daily, 8 mg oral hydromorphone daily, or an equianalgesic dose of another opioid daily for at least 1 week (approval criterion 3). Dose equivalence and duration documentation require manual review.

Approval criterion 5 (notes only): patients and providers must comply with the TIRF REMS ACCESS program if applicable. https://www.tirfremsaccess.com/TirfUI/rems/home.action . Dispensing to outpatients requires program enrollment; patient enrollment is not required for inpatient administration (including hospitals, hospices and long-term care facilities prescribing for inpatient use). No REMS predicate is added.
Authorization: up to 6 months. Dispensing limit: 30-day supply. These limits remain notes only and require manual review.

Contraindicated in opioid non-tolerant patients and for acute or postoperative pain; life-threatening respiratory depression and death may occur. Closed indication and opioid tolerance predicates cover these exclusions.
Intended for oncologists and pain specialists knowledgeable and skilled in Schedule II opioids for cancer pain. Prescriber specialty is notes only, not an approval predicate.
Remaining gaps: REMS compliance, authorization duration, dispensing enforcement and documentation verification. Rules engine is the sole eligibility evaluator.
